# <span id="aanchor216"></span> Meter Quick Create

Meter Quick Create is a quick and simple way to quickly create a new gas meter or multiple gas meters that share one or more common attributes.  This allows the user to set up the import driver and import path (file and folder name) so that the user does not have to enter it every time he or she wants to import data for a meter.  This screen also allows the user to add more information about the meter such as: characteristics, units (US or Metric), the user can set validations and select information that the user would want to have on a report.

This function is not available for liquid meters and may not be available for gas meters if the administrator has set up required meter fields and disabled Meter Quick Create.

<div class="procedure">

To create a meter:

1.  Go to **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Quick Create**.

2.  When a meter is created or edited, some fields can be required to be populated. Failure to populate a required field will prevent a record from being saved. Required fields that are blank are highlighted in green.

    There are numerous fields in the Meter Attributes that are not available under Meter Quick Create and meters can thus be created without all of the required fields being populated. Once you edit the meter under the Meter Editor, then the remaining required fields must be populated before you can save any other changes.

3.  Under the Imports tab, select an Import Driver (see: [Import Driver Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/Import%20Driver%20Editor.md)) from the drop-down menu or click to add a new import driver.

    Depending on what import driver you choose, the fields may change on the screen.  For example, if you select Bristol as your import driver, the fields for an FCS File and Shared CFG will appear. If Fisher import driver is selected, the field TUBE NUMBER will appear.

4.  Enter an import path.

5.  Enter a file name.

6.  Click the **Save** button.

7.  To enter more meters, click **Clear** and repeat steps 1-6. Alternatively, the user may elect to enter only values for fields common across multiple new meter to be created and the user must only enter a new meter number and click **Save**.

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Imports Tab">

The following items are available on the Imports tab:

- **Compare to Master Characteristics** - If Compare to Master Characteristics is checked, FLOWCAL will check to see if the meters characteristics match the Master Characteristics. If the Master Characteristics are different from the meter characteristics, an exception will occur. Exceptions and updates of characteristics will be done based on user selection within the Master Data Validation.
- **External Volume** - An External Volume Meter is usually a meter whose volume is not calculated in the System.  The meter's data is imported into FLOWCAL via the External Volume Import Mechanism (Data Entry or File Import) where it can be edited and utilized with complete reporting functions.
- **Update Meter Name** - Normally, the meter name from the .CFX file associated with a meter is imported into FLOWCAL, unless the user has this field set to NO. The meter name in the field is not always what is desired in FLOWCAL. By default, the meter name is updated on import with the meter name from the field. If you want to keep the meter name manually entered into FLOWCAL, set this field to "No."
- **Inhibit Default Exceptions** - If set to Yes, FLOWCAL will not generate any exceptions for default validations. FLOWCAL runs an extensive suite of Default Validations to alert the user about data being out of range for a given calculation or configuration. User configured validations will still generate exceptions. By default, this field is set to Null. Null and No are treated the same.
- **Auto Edit Criteria** - This option can set a particular Auto Edit at the meter level. Auto Edit Criterian= also has the ability to be enabled only at Import.
- **Import ID** - Import ID is used for text file imports, Transaction Queue processing and also for imports of Flow Automation MBS## files. If importing text files or Transaction Queue data, the meter number in the system sending data to FLOWCAL may not match the meter number in the user's system. If so, put the meter number from the other system in Import ID and check the box Meter number field is Import ID when importing the text file. If Importing MBS## files, there is a requirement that the meter name in FLOWCAL match that in the MBS## file. If you want a different meter name in FLOWCAL, put the meter name of the meter in the MBS## file in the Import ID field.
- **Snap Before and Snap After** - The Snap Before and Snap After fields are used to snap data to the start of an hour. When dealing with hourly data, records are expected to come in right on the hour. Sometimes the records may come in with a time stamp that is before or after the hour it is for. For example, the 9:00 record might come in with a time stamp of 9:00:03 or 8:59:19. This will cause the user's missing data report to flag data as missing and gaps will appear in the hourly view of data. If this record is supposed to be at the top of the hour, you can specify how before or after the start of the hour a record can come in and have it moved to the top of the hour. No revision is created in the hourly data, so there is no way to see the shift in data. The total of the time before the start of the hour and after the end of the hour cannot exceed the number of seconds specified for data resolution in the meter characteristics (3600 for hourly data, 900 for 15 minute data). If there are multiple records that meet the criteria, the first record will be flagged at the top of the hour, and the next record will be one second after (or before for time trails data). (See: [Snap Before/Snap After Details](../Meter%20Editor/Snap%20Before-Snap%20After.md))
- **FCS File** - This is the mapping file (3308, 3530, teleflow, etc) of how the Bristol is formed.
- **Shared CFG** - Used only on a multitube where the CFG is shared among the two.
- **Tube Number** - Used only with the Fisher to designate the appropriate meter run inside .AGA or .DET files (300, 400, 500 series).
- **Entry Number** - Entry Number is used with Flow Automation Meters only. If the user leaves this blank it will automatically pick the last entry within the file.
- **Option 1 & 2** - The user may need to enter data for options 1 and 2 (depending on what type of import driver is chosen).  These fields are used if different flow computers are configured to interface with FLOWCAL. See ‘Import Driver Settings’ for more information.
- **Import CFX Units** - Units for fields such as volume, energy, temperature and pressure can be included in CFX files. Older CFX creation programs may not properly populate these fields. The user should Check Import CFX Units if his or her CFX files will have the valid units that the user wants FLOWCAL to import.
- **Create Revisions** - When data is imported into FLOWCAL, if data has previously been imported for a date and time, data on subsequent imports will be ignored, even if the data is different. The only way to get this data in is to purge the record. If Create Revisions is checked, when new data is imported, the previous data is retained, but the new data will be saved in the next available revision. For example, if there is record at 9:00 and there was an edit done creating a revision 1 record, the next import with different data for the 9:00 record will cause the creation of a rev. 2 record with the new data. If a subsequent import has the same data as was previously imported, no additional records are created.
- **Ignore Configuration Snapshot** - If Ignore Configuration Snapshot is selected, FLOWCAL will update the Meter Configuration based on events only; otherwise, the CFX configuration or transaction snap shots will be used as a check sum to compare to the database meter configuration. Any discrepancies will be updated to reflect CFX or transaction snapshot values.

If yes is selected, a lost event will cause FLOWCAL to reflect the wrong value with no automated means of detection. This feature is to accommodate collection or "polling engines" who do not properly collect the "snapshot" when gathering the data.
